slides.big_en: A ḥadīth is short: read it slowly, word by word.
slides.big_ar: اِقْرَأْ ثُمَّ اسْأَلْ: عَنْ مَاذَا يَتَكَلَّمُ؟
slides.small: First find the topic (what it is about), then what is said about it. Most of these sayings are two-part sentences with no verb.
slides.small_ar: اِبْحَثْ أَوَّلًا عَنِ الْمُبْتَدَأِ، ثُمَّ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ. أَكْثَرُ هَذِهِ الْجُمَلِ بِلَا فِعْلٍ.

lines: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Religion is sincere advice.”
He said: “For Allah, for His Book and for His Messenger …”
The believer is, for the believer, like a building,
one part of it strengthening another.

gloss: charity, a gift to do good

lines: Which sayings have NO verb at all? (Only a topic and a statement.)
أَيُّ الْجُمَلِ بِلَا فِعْلٍ؟ (مُبْتَدَأٌ وَخَبَرٌ فَقَطْ)
In الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ both words have ال. Which one is the topic?
فِي «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ» كَلِمَتَانِ فِيهِمَا ال. أَيُّهُمَا الْمُبْتَدَأُ؟
Which word tells you “like” in the second ḥadīth? Which word tells you “one part … another”?
فِي الْحَدِيثِ الثَّانِي: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُفِيدُ التَّشْبِيهَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَدُلَّانِ عَلَى جُزْءٍ وَجُزْءٍ آخَرَ؟

slides.head_en: Most of these sayings are a topic + a statement

cards.def_en: what it is about: has ال, ends in ـُ
what is said about it: tanwīn (ـٌ)
a small joiner stuck to the next word

slides.why: A student writes نُورًا. Wrong! After a plain topic the statement ends in ـٌ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ. (ـًا comes only after كَانَ and لَيْسَ.)
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ «نُورًا». خَطَأٌ! بَعْدَ الْمُبْتَدَأِ يَنْتَهِي الْخَبَرُ بِـ ـٌ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.

lines: جَلَسَ وَلَدٌ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَسَمِعَ طَالِبًا حَزِينًا.
A boy sat in the mosque, and he heard a sad student.
The boy said to the student: You are my friend.
كَانَتِ الْكَلِمَةُ طَيِّبَةً، وَكَانَ الطَّالِبُ سَعِيدًا.
The word was kind, and the student was happy.
قَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ، وَالْأَدَبُ جَمِيلٌ.
The teacher said: Knowledge is light, and good manners are beautiful.
شَكَرَ الطَّالِبُ الْوَلَدَ وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ.
The student thanked the boy and returned to the ribāṭ.
